title: Claude's recommended dev workflow
subtitle: The skills Claude would want loaded across a code project from kickoff to production. Start with Common; layer specialised tracks (Backend / Frontend / Mobile / Data·ML) on top when they apply.
note: Each pick cites an exemplar from the corpus when one exists. Click it to read the actual skill.

tracks.name: Common
tracks.tagline: Works for any code project. The baseline every track inherits.

phases.name: 1. Kick off
phases.summary: Sharpen a vague idea into a concrete requirements doc and a working scaffold. Most rework comes from skipping this step.

picks.why: Forces you to articulate constraints, non-goals, and 'when NOT to use it' before any code. Saves hours of mid-implementation pivots.
Gets the boring initial work right: .gitignore, CI stub, README skeleton, project conventions. Turns 'set up day' into 'set up hour'.

picks.concept: Codebase audit (when joining an existing project)
picks.why: Maps the landscape — modules, hot spots, conventions — before you touch anything. Prevents naive edits that violate hidden invariants.

phases.name: 2. Plan
phases.summary: Decompose the work, lock down architecture, write the decisions you'll regret forgetting later.

picks.why: PRD → design review → tech decisions → research → metrics. Each gate forces clarity before the next. Half the bugs are killed before they exist.
Scores the design against principles like 'action parity' and 'tools as primitives'. Catches anti-patterns before they're load-bearing.

phases.name: 3. Build
phases.summary: Small loops, deterministic outputs, frequent checkpoints. Trust the spec from the plan phase.

picks.why: Splits big tasks across many subagents working in parallel. Keeps individual changes small and reviewable instead of one mega-diff.
Translates the plan into concrete, ordered steps with verification between each. The discipline pays off in late-stage debugging.

phases.name: 4. Verify
phases.summary: Correctness, performance, and security before anything ships. Reviews catch what tests can't.

picks.why: Looks at correctness bugs AND reuse / simplification / efficiency in one pass. Faster than waiting for a human review round-trip.
Hits the user-facing flow after each meaningful change. Catches integration regressions that unit tests miss by design.

phases.name: 5. Ship
phases.summary: Clean up, document, announce. The work isn't done until someone else can use it.

picks.why: Prunes stale branches and clarifies what's in flight. A clean repo is faster to navigate the next morning.
Markdown + Mermaid for architecture, flows, decision trees. Future-you and your teammates will thank present-you.
GIF / terminal recording / screenshots showing the change actually works. Reviewers grok intent in 5 seconds vs reading 500 lines.

phases.name: 6. Operate
phases.summary: Production starts on deploy. Watch the signals you said you'd watch.

picks.why: Tails the relevant dashboards and alerts for N minutes after deploy. Catches the regression while you still remember what changed.
Periodically summarizes what users experienced, how the product performed, and which signals deserve a closer look. Stops bugs from compounding silently.

tracks.name: Backend
tracks.note: Read Common first. These layer on server-side specifics.

phases.name: 2. Plan
phases.summary: API + data model first; decide write paths and consistency story before any controller code.

picks.why: Define OpenAPI / gRPC proto / SDL schema before writing handlers. Server and client codegen + contract tests both build on this single source.
Tables, relationships, indexes — and most importantly access patterns — drawn out before any migration runs. Saves expensive late-stage rewrites.

phases.name: 3. Build
phases.summary: Migrations and request shape are where production usually breaks first. Be strict.

picks.why: Additive-only migrations (add column → backfill → switch reads → remove old). Every migration must have a rollback path. Never DROP in the same release as the read switch.
Schema-validate every inbound request (Zod / Pydantic / proto). Reject early with clear errors instead of letting bad data leak into the persistence layer.

phases.name: 4. Verify
phases.summary: Beyond unit tests: hammer the API like real clients will.

picks.why: k6 / Locust / wrk against staging with realistic traffic shape. p95/p99 latency, tail behaviour, connection pool exhaustion — better found here than at 3 AM.
Diff the actual implementation against the API contract on every PR. Catches breaking changes before clients see them.

phases.name: 6. Operate
phases.summary: Servers run 24/7. Observability is not a launch checklist item — it's the operational primitive.

picks.why: JSON logs with request_id + OpenTelemetry spans across services. Without these you debug production by reading tea leaves.
Separate user-visible errors from internal noise. Burn-rate alerts on the SLO let you know when something's actually wrong vs background flakes.

tracks.name: Frontend
tracks.note: Read Common first. These layer on frontend specifics.

phases.name: 1. Kick off
phases.summary: Audit what already exists in the design system. Don't reinvent buttons.

picks.why: List every existing token, primitive, and pattern before creating new ones. 80% of 'new components' should be assemblies of existing primitives.

phases.name: 2. Plan
phases.summary: Wireframes precede pixel-perfect designs precede code. Skipping a layer makes the next one painful.

picks.why: Clickable, low-fidelity prototype before any component code. Faster to throw away when the UX is wrong.
Props, slots, controlled vs uncontrolled — sketched on paper before TypeScript. Sane defaults > more options.

phases.name: 3. Build
phases.summary: Build in isolation, integrate last. Storybook is leverage.

picks.why: Develop each component against its stories, not by tabbing to the live app. Smaller feedback loop = faster iteration.

phases.name: 4. Verify
phases.summary: Pixels matter, accessibility matters, performance matters. Automate each.

picks.why: Snapshot diff (Percy / Chromatic / Playwright) catches the 'we accidentally broke the header on mobile' bug before users do.
axe / pa11y in CI + manual keyboard / screen reader pass before launch. Roughly 15% of users benefit; 100% of code reviews should require it.
Same Playwright/Cypress suite from Common; for frontend work this is where most regressions surface.

phases.name: 5. Ship
phases.summary: Don't ship 5MB of JavaScript for a button.

picks.why: Track bundle size budget per route. Lighthouse perf/a11y/SEO scores in CI. Regressions blocked at PR time.

phases.name: 6. Operate
phases.summary: Users hit weird browser versions, weird network conditions, weird input devices. See it from their side.

picks.why: Sentry / LogRocket capturing JS errors + session replay. Source maps uploaded so stacks are readable. Cumulative Layout Shift alerts too.
RUM (real user monitoring) for LCP, INP, CLS by route. Lab numbers lie; production p75s don't.

tracks.name: Mobile
tracks.note: Read Common first. Mobile adds device + store specifics.

phases.name: 2. Plan
phases.summary: The cross-platform decision is the most expensive one to reverse. Make it explicit and document why.

picks.why: Write an ADR. Constraints: team skills, performance ceiling, OS-specific features needed, time-to-market. Don't drift into one because of momentum.

phases.name: 3. Build
phases.summary: Tight build/simulate loop matters more on mobile — IDE+simulator dance kills focus.

picks.why: One command to build + boot simulator + install + launch + tail logs. Cuts the 30-second context switch each iteration.

phases.name: 4. Verify
phases.summary: Your phone isn't the user's phone.

picks.why: iPhone SE through iPhone Pro Max, Pixel 4a through Galaxy S24, OS N-2 through N. Cloud device farms (BrowserStack/Sauce) for breadth, physical for touch feel.

phases.name: 5. Ship
phases.summary: Store reviewers reject weird things. Be ready.

picks.why: Privacy manifest, permission justifications, age rating, screenshots for every device class, release notes, what's-new copy. Treat as a deploy artifact.

phases.name: 6. Operate
phases.summary: Mobile users update slowly. Old versions linger.

picks.why: Crash-free rate per app version. Funnel analytics for the critical user paths. Forced-update gate for unfixable old versions.

tracks.name: Data / ML
tracks.tagline: Data pipelines, model training, scientific computing.
tracks.note: Read Common first. Data / ML adds eval-set discipline and reproducibility.

phases.name: 1. Kick off
phases.summary: Look at the data before assuming anything.

picks.why: Read the actual schema, sample rows, distributions. Nulls, encoding, time-zone bugs, label imbalance — these become 80% of project pain if found late.

phases.name: 2. Plan
phases.summary: The evaluation set is the project's truth. Build it before any model.

picks.why: Held-out test set + slices for sub-populations + the dumb-baseline number. If you can't articulate the metric and how it's measured, you're not ready to train.

phases.name: 3. Build
phases.summary: Notebooks are great for exploration, bad for production. Convert at the right moment.

picks.why: Once a notebook 'works', extract into a script with locked seeds, pinned deps, deterministic outputs. The notebook stays for exploration; the script is what runs in CI.
K-Dense-AI's collection covers most common ground (zarr for chunked arrays, geomaster for geospatial, fluidsim for CFD, etc.). Reuse before reinventing.

phases.name: 4. Verify
phases.summary: Models lie smoothly. Compare against baselines, watch for drift.

picks.why: Random / most-frequent-class / last-value-carried-forward — your model must beat the dumb baseline on every metric and slice. If it doesn't, you have a bug.
Compare train vs prod feature distributions periodically. PSI / KL-divergence alerts on the inputs catch silent degradation before metrics tank.

phases.name: 5. Ship
phases.summary: Models without provenance can't be reproduced, can't be audited.

picks.why: What was trained on what data, with what splits, evaluated how, with which limitations. Future-you and your auditors both need this.
Pipeline diagrams (data → features → model → output) make a system reviewable. Mermaid is enough; you don't need draw.io.

phases.name: 6. Operate
phases.summary: Inference cost and latency are now business metrics.

picks.why: Tokens per request, p95/p99 latency, cost per query. Especially with LLM-backed features, cost can spike from a single prompt regression.
